name: Leicester City 2015/16 (Claudio Ranieri)
scopeNote: Leicester City, Premier League champions 2015/16 under Claudio Ranieri (managerId claudio-ranieri, appointed 2015-07-13). Period = first competitive match (Premier League opener v Sunderland, 8 Aug 2015, from OffTheBall) to last (final-day 1-1 at Chelsea, FourFourTwo; the date 15 May 2016 comes from a premierleague.com preview title and search results, not a mined page). League Cup and FA Cup games fall inside this window but were not researched individually. Style term used by sources: a compact 4-4-2 that became a 4-4-1-1 out of possession (Premier League/Opta), zonal marking with man-orientations (Spielverlagerung: 'zone-orientated man coverage'), counter-attack/transition game at 42.43% possession. Popular label 'catenaccio' is rejected by SI. 'Low block' is only partly right: Spielverlagerung says mid-low block and FourFourTwo says default is sitting deep in own third with higher pressing when needed, while SI says the back line is high enough to catch forwards offside.
openQuestions: Block height: Spielverlagerung (Feb and Apr 2016) says mid-low block and that Huth/Morgan lack speed for a higher line; FourFourTwo Stats Zone says default is sitting deep and waiting inside own third; SI (Dec 2015) says line high enough to catch forwards offside and Leicester wants to 'press high'. Both can be true at different moments (SI describes Dec 2015, sample of 3 matches for Schmeichel). Treat as mid-low block with selective pressing triggers (ball moves wide, Kante as trigger).
Set-pieces: only the aggregate (17 set-piece goals, second in league) and anecdotal Ulloa/Huth/Morgan threat found; no source on zonal vs man marking at corners for 2015/16 and no routine analysis.
Last match date 2016-05-15 not read from a mined page (premierleague.com preview title and several search results only).
Coaches' Voice, These Football Times, Zonal Marking (Cox), Jonathan Wilson, StatsBomb and a Corriere della Sera Italian original not found; PPDA/pressing-height data not found.
Number of players used: sources differ (23 per Sports Mole; Stats Perform says 18 starters after 31 games); not used as verified.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: The Italian made the switch to a compact 4-4-2 system built to counter-attack with devastating efficiency.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: Leicester, who had used 11 different formations the year before, stuck with this 4-4-2, which became a 4-4-1-1 out of possession, in 35 of their 38 matches.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: His plan was to operate with two disciplined banks of four, with an energetic deep-lying striker operating behind a speedy centre-forward, who could punish opponents on the break.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: Realising their goal threat was enhanced by game plans that revolved around transitions, Leicester are the only champions to have adopted a non-possession-based strategy.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: Their average possession figure (42.43 per cent) is by some distance the lowest on record for a Premier League winning team, since such data started being collected in 2003/04.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: When you compare the Foxes' numbers from 2014/15 and 2015/16 it is surprising to note that there was not a major shift in terms of shots, shots faced or the amount of possession they enjoyed.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: During an astonishing campaign in which they lost only three times, Ranieri made just 33 changes to his starting XI.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: What we witnessed that season was a very special collective effort that enabled an experienced team to produce peak efficiency in the defensive, middle and final thirds.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: On those fast breaks the brilliance of Riyad Mahrez, who scored 17 goals and added 11 assists, and Jamie Vardy (24 goals, six assists) regularly made the difference.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: The Foxes' resolute defensive shape proved hard to break down. And rival teams, perhaps showing a degree of complacency, continued to leave themselves open to counter-attacks.

sources.title: PL30: How Ranieri masterminded Leicester's title victory
sources.evidence: Ranieri's relaxed demeanour took the pressure off his players, who went on to ride a spectacular and unexpected wave for the entirety of a season that will never be forgotten.

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Ranieri’s side have been a welcome change in the Premier League as they employ a zonal marking system with man-orientations which sees them stay stable and compact in a 4-4-1-1 shape.

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: When not tasked with covering a nearby attacker, the team will maintain their shape in their base positions and cover the space in a zonal structure. However when a forward moves within a defender’s vicinity they will flexibly orient themselves within their space to cover this player by keeping a certain distance away from them where they can apply pressure on a position level.

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: Leicester’s compactness must also be noted as it plays an important role in their organisation. Through the zonal scheme they maintain their shape and do so with strong distances both horizontally and vertically.

sources.title: Arsenal - Leicester City 2:1 (Spielverlagerung)

sources.title: Leicester City: Smart as eleven foxes (Spielverlagerung)
sources.evidence: In the first phase of pressing, both forwards move laterally a lot, switching between the opposing players they are asked to man-mark in what is zone-orientated man coverage. The midfield line, meanwhile, moves in regards to the ball position and always keeps the initial shape. Only one of the wingers pushes a few yards forward if the opposing team move the ball to his side.

sources.title: Leicester City: Smart as eleven foxes (Spielverlagerung)

sources.evidence: The Foxes line up in a standard English 4-4-2, with Riyad Mahrez’s tendency to drift inside and next to the front two passing as their most complicated wrinkle.

sources.title: Tactical breakdown: How Ranieri's Leicester City has overtaken the EPL (SI)

sources.title: Tactical breakdown: How Ranieri's Leicester City has overtaken the EPL (SI)
